What book should I hear about and then not bother reading?
What's a commonly referenced book that you read and think is far over-rated?
Most religious texts are over-rated. I haven't read the Koran yet, but as soon as I have I'll report back here. In the meantime, I can report that the Bhagavad Gita is utter shite.

The Kingkiller Chronicles.

People at Reddit cannot stop jerking themselves off about this book series.

It's a series about an unreliable narrator that frequently does the impossible. Reddit defends the main character Mary Sue through the guise of the unreliable narrator.

Personally I find it to be bullshit. I can't stand it. Couldn't even finish the first book.

Pride and Prejudice.

I read about a quarter way through, as a blank slate, and the other quarter was a solid grind until I gave up and hoped they all died of dysentery.

Anything by Neil Gaiman or Steven King.

Pick one book by King and read it. Congratulations. You've now read every book by King. Just imagine different monsters and settings. You've also read every book by Gaiman at that point. Just imagine the King book you read was dressed up in a lot of unnecessary, ambiguous, whimsical imagery.

King is fine if your selective about it, his first few books didn't quite go down the redundant path.

Carrie, The Shining, The Stand, and the first Dark Tower book all stand on their own pretty well. It's with IT, that you really begin the coming of age horror story trope he's known for.

Edit. Also Salem's Lot. Carrie and Salem's Lot are throw backs in styling so to speak. Carrie is largely told through interviews and news paper clippings by the end and Salem's Lot is a Dracula retelling in small town Maine I think.

Anything Dickens. Paid by the word = hack.

The Stand. King's best work is short stories. His novels would most benefit from a ruthless editor.

The Grapes of Wrath and everything else I was forced to read in high school.

Game of Thrones... it's good, don't get me wrong, but over hyped to hell and back.

No one has said Neal Stephenson so far thankfully.
